name: Hand-timed lightning strike: thick bolt, thin line, mirrored bolt, black afterimage frame, evaporating segments

source.title: Dan Root, How to Animate a Lightning Strike (2D animation, YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: hold, then one frame of only the jagged start at the top plus a small spark ON THE GROUND where it will hit (the ground conducts first)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: 24 fps, 1-2 frames each: thick filled S-bolt (held 2 frames) -> the same bolt in BLACK (afterimage) -> a thin line on the same path -> the bolt MIRRORED (curves flipped) thick -> thin line

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: the line breaks into short segments, then only tiny end bits remain = energy evaporating down the path; then empty frames

layers.motion: one loose S from sky to target, two outlines with alternating thickness and sharp elbows, a few sparky side bits; regenerate as the MIRRORED path every other frame
layers.notes: thick/thin alternation and sharp elbows read as dangerous

layers.motion: the bolt silhouette drawn black for exactly one frame right after a white frame
layers.notes: black after white burns an afterimage; use one frame, small area (photosensitivity)

layers.motion: blue glow around every bolt frame
layers.notes: glow filter on all frames

layers.motion: small spark shape at the ground contact one frame before the bolt
layers.notes: anticipation tells where it will land

layers.motion: path split into dashes, then only the dash ends, then gone (2 frames each)
layers.notes: fade by changing state, not by lowering alpha

whyItLooksGood: frame-level timing: lightning lives on 1-2 frame holds, never a smooth tween
mirroring the shape between frames gives flicker and drama without new art
a mid-grey background makes the white bolt and the black frame both read
buildNotes: Use LightningArc (parts kit) with a fixed seed per beat: frame list [thick A x2, black A, thin A, thick mirror(A), thin mirror(A), dashes, dash-ends]; step on a 1/24 s clock, not dt-smooth. Ground spark: StarBurst at the hit point one frame early.

name: Stylised bolt from a concept image: crisp + glow channels, pinched ends, and a black outline ribbon behind it

source.title: CGHOW (Ashif Ali), From Concept to VFX: Stylized Lightning in UE5 Niagara (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: impact
phases.what: a blue bolt crawls from sky to target, both ends pinched to a point; a dark outline hugs it

phases.name: release
phases.what: re-spawns with random axis and very short life (~0.12 s) so it flickers; purple glowing disc of hex cells on the ground (from the concept)

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: last bolt fades, ground disc dims

layers.motion: ribbon/beam with a tileable bolt texture scrolling along it; R channel = crisp bolt (white core), G channel = blurred glow (tinted); ends pinched by a sine mask along the length
layers.notes: one texture, two channels: core and glow

layers.motion: duplicate of the same ribbon (same random path), black, a bit wider/more alpha, drawn BEHIND the blue one
layers.notes: the black outline makes the bolt pop on any background — black is a colour

layers.motion: glowing disc of hex/cell shapes at the strike point
layers.notes: taken from the concept image

layers.motion: colour noise + jitter on the bolt, short life 0.12 s, random axis per spawn
layers.notes: flicker comes from re-spawning, not from blinking alpha

whyItLooksGood: concept first: an image fixes colour and shape before any tech
dark outline + white core + tinted glow = a full value ladder on a thin shape
pinched ends stop the bolt looking like a pasted strip
buildNotes: Two LightningArc meshes sharing one path: back one black, normal blend, width x1.4; front one additive white core + blue glow. Pinch width with sin(pi*t) along the path. Re-roll the path every 0.12 s.

name: Layered stylised laser: dark under-beam, scrolling eroded core, electric tendrils, stretched sparks and a source flare

source.title: Gabriel Aguiar Prod., Unity VFX Graph Stylized Laser Beam (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: release
phases.what: the beam LENGTH shoots out from the source in 10% of life (pivot at the source), width pops in

phases.name: channel
phases.what: video 0:30 hero: violet beam with a dark core underneath, streaky texture scrolling toward the target, distortion wobble, blue electric tendrils crawling, sparks streaking along it, flashes popping at the source

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: width shrinks to 0 over the last 10% of life

layers.motion: very dark red copy, 1.5x wider, drawn FIRST
layers.notes: dark under-beam gives contrast; same scale curves as the core

layers.motion: seamless streak texture scrolling at speed 2 toward the target, x end-fade mask (0 -> 100% -> 60% -> 0 along the length), UV distortion = lerp(uv, noise, 0.15) with noise scrolling faster (3)
layers.notes: texture: one big wrap-mode stroke with the inside erased at 40% and smudged tendrils

layers.motion: copy of the core in blue with a high alpha clip (eroded to tendrils) and more distortion (0.2-0.3)
layers.notes: electric layer for almost no extra work

layers.motion: spawn 40/s in a small circle at the source, velocity along the beam 20-40, life 0.2-0.45 s, stretched along velocity, size big -> small
layers.notes: fast streaks sell speed

layers.motion: soft flashes at the source, life 0.1-0.2 s, size 2.5-5 big -> small, repeated through the duration
layers.notes: pulsing source keeps the hold alive

whyItLooksGood: a single DURATION drives every layer, so they all start and end together
grow length fast, shrink width slow at the end: the beam feels shot, then spent
dark under-layer + bright core + eroded electric copy = depth from three copies of one shape
buildNotes: Plane mesh with its pivot at the source, billboarded around the beam axis; scale.y curve 0->1 by 10% life, scale.x 0->1 fast and 1->0 from 90%. Three copies (dark normal, core additive, electric eroded) + Emitter streaks along the axis + GlowSphere pulses at the source.

name: Refraction bubble shield: twirl-distorted screen behind it, fresnel + intersection rim, hit dimple and edge dissolve

source.title: A Bit Of Game Dev, Unity Shader Graph Bubble Shield (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: bubble materialises: edge-glow dissolve sweeping bottom -> top

phases.name: channel
phases.what: video 0:04: blue fresnel rim, the world behind seen through a slow twirl distortion (clear in the centre, swirling toward the rim), bright line where it cuts the ground; each hit pushes a dimple in at the hit point and magnifies there

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: dissolves away with a glowing edge

layers.motion: screen texture sampled at screenPos + twirled rotating Voronoi offset, masked by distance from the disc centre (clear middle)
layers.notes: refraction sells 'glass' more than colour does

layers.motion: fresnel rim (power), front faces only
layers.notes: rim carries the silhouette

layers.motion: bright intersection line where the sphere meets the ground/objects (depth difference smoothstep)
layers.notes: grounds the bubble

layers.motion: on hit: sphere-mask at the hit point drives a vertex push inward (curve: in fast, wobble back) and a local magnify
layers.notes: localised feedback instead of a whole-shell flash

layers.motion: height-gradient + noise dissolve with a second offset threshold = glowing edge band, bottom -> top
layers.notes: fade by changing state

whyItLooksGood: the shield changes what is BEHIND it (refraction), not just adds light
hits are local (dimple at the impact point) so the shield feels physical
intersection line ties it to the floor
buildNotes: three.js: render the scene to a target first (or use the composer's previous buffer) and sample it in the bubble material with a twirl offset; fresnel term for alpha/emissive; on hit set a uniform hitPos and animate a displacement amount; dissolve with a world-Y gradient + noise threshold and an edge band. Cheaper fallback: GlowSphere rim + a rotating swirl texture.

name: Swirl portal disc: polar-spun noise x twirled Voronoi over a soft circular mask

source.title: Flex Unit, Stylized Portal VFX in Unity, Shader Graph (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: disc scales open from a point with overshoot

phases.name: channel
phases.what: video 9:05: pale blue-white disc, darker spiral streaks rotating inward, soft feathered rim

layers.motion: noise in polar UVs rotating over time, multiplied by a twirled Voronoi; blended with a soft circular base texture; alpha from the base texture
layers.notes: spin + twirl gives the inward pull

layers.motion: faint glow halo around the rim
layers.notes: keeps the edge soft

layers.motion: optional: motes spiralling into the centre
layers.notes: not in the video; adds the inward read in 3D

whyItLooksGood: two noises in different coordinate systems (polar spin, twirled cells) never repeat visibly
the dark spiral streaks give the bright disc depth
buildNotes: One plane with a small ShaderMaterial: polar uv (r, a + t*speed), noise(r*k, a*n) * twirledVoronoi, times a smoothstep circle mask; scale-in with overshoot. Pairs with the summon archetype (something steps out).

name: Wind tornado from a twisted, off-centre funnel mesh with scrolling texture, colour ramp and spinning ground waves

source.title: Le Lu, Godot 3D VFX Tornado Effect (Wind) (YouTube tutorial)

phases.name: anticipation
phases.what: ground waves spin up and opacity of the funnel ramps in

phases.name: channel
phases.what: video 0:12: blue-white twisted funnel spinning (-360 deg per 0.8 s) with the texture scrolling the opposite way; lightning arcs around it; ground swirl of waves and sparks

phases.name: aftermath
phases.what: opacity / alpha-clip threshold fades the funnel out; waves die

layers.motion: hollow 24-sided funnel, flared top and bottom, BASE pushed off-centre (curvature), top twisted hard; texture scroll (-1.2, 2); minus a clamped vertical gradient to kill the ends; colour/alpha from a 1D ramp sampled by the texture value
layers.notes: the twist makes any scrolled texture follow the spiral

layers.motion: small twisted-cylinder 'wave' meshes at the base: zero gravity, up 0-3, random angle, life 0.5 s, scale small -> big, angular velocity, alpha-clip dissolve; duplicate at the top in local space
layers.notes: hides the hard floor intersection, which players see up close

layers.motion: a few arcs flicking around the funnel
layers.notes: storm flavour (seen in the hero shot)

layers.motion: sparks swirling on the ground ring
layers.notes: secondary

whyItLooksGood: an off-centre base and a twisted top make a static mesh look alive when it spins
colour comes from a ramp driven by the texture, so one texture gives core and edge colours
for mobile/VR: alpha-clip instead of transparency avoids overdraw and still looks like wind
buildNotes: Build the funnel as a LatheGeometry with a twist applied per ring (rotate each ring by k*height) and the bottom ring offset in x; ShaderMaterial with scrolling noise, end-fade gradient and a ramp; spin the mesh, scroll UVs the other way. Ground waves: InstancedMesh of short twisted rings with scale/alpha curves.
